anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : The optimizer persistently chooses sub-optimal execution plans despite having reasonably accurate statistics.
MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly : Obsolete row versions and rollback data accumulate faster than background cleanup can reclaim them, inflating storage and visibility-check overhead.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : Network, listener, socket, or authentication resources become saturated, slowing or preventing client connections and data transfer.

When these three root causes strike together, the database exhibits extreme and hard-to-pinpoint performance degradation. Poorly chosen plans trigger long-running scans or nested-loop explosions that touch far more rows than expected; the excess I/O and CPU prolong transaction lifetimes, causing snapshots to remain open and preventing version cleanup. The resulting table and index bloat further pollute statistics and widen the gap between estimated and actual costs, encouraging the optimizer to continue selecting bad plans. Meanwhile, the oversized result sets and elongated execution times keep back-end processes and sockets busy, filling connection pools, exhausting listener backlogs, and amplifying network queuing delays, retransmissions, and connection-establishment failures. Observability signals therefore include rapidly growing table sizes and version-store length, erratic plan changes with soaring execution costs, rising client-side timeouts, half-open connections, and a mix of in-database (buffer-read, MVCC visibility check) waits and network I/O waits.

Causally, a feedback loop emerges: (1) Sub-optimal plans inflate row access counts and execution duration. (2) Prolonged transactions retain old snapshots, blocking vacuum/cleanup and accelerating MVCC version bloat. (3) The swollen heap and misestimated cardinalities drive the optimizer toward even worse plans, perpetuating step 1. (4) Larger result sets and longer server think-time keep connections occupied, pushing the network and listener layer to saturation, which in turn delays new sessions and retries, increasing concurrency spikes. (5) Connection stalls further lengthen transaction lifetimes, intensifying MVCC retention and plan misestimation. Together, these intertwined effects degrade throughput, inflate latency, and threaten availability in high-churn transactional environments.

entry.error_class: Class 42 - Syntax Error or Access Rule Violation
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with unsupported syntax, invalid statement structure, or feature usage that the target engine version cannot execute as written.
entry.solution_guidance: Validate SQL syntax, target-engine compatibility, statement shape, and whether the feature is supported under the current engine version or execution context.
